Eastern Cape heatwave: Which areas are affected and how long will it last?
SAWS warns of a three-day heatwave in parts of the Eastern Cape from Thursday, with persistently high temperatures expected until Saturday.
The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a heatwave advisory for parts of the Eastern Cape.
It was warning residents to prepare for several days of persistently high temperatures.
The heatwave will affect places in the Inxuba Yethemba Local Municipality from Thursday, until Saturday.
Which areas will experience the heatwave?
The advisory covers parts of Inxuba Yethemba Local Municipality, which includes Cradock and Middelburg in the Eastern Cape.
SAWS expects temperatures to remain unusually high in affected areas for three consecutive days.
The advisory does not specify exact temperatures or identify which parts of the municipality will experience the highest readings.
Why is a heatwave different from a hot day?
A heatwave brings unusually high temperatures over several consecutive days, rather than just one hot afternoon.
When the heat continues for several days, people may struggle to cool down, particularly if temperatures remain high indoors or overnight.
Prolonged exposure to heat can also increase the risk of dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.
How can residents stay safe?
Residents should drink water regularly, avoid spending long periods in direct sunlight and avoid outdoor activities during the hottest parts of the day.
People who work outdoors should take regular breaks in shaded or cooler areas.
Older people, young children and those with existing health conditions may be particularly vulnerable to prolonged heat.
Residents should also check on vulnerable family members and neighbours.
When will the heatwave end?
SAWS expects the heatwave conditions to continue until Saturday, 31 October.
However, the advisory does not confirm how quickly temperatures will drop afterwards.
Residents should continue checking the latest SAWS forecasts and advisories for any changes.
